functions.name: send
functions.description: Send a message as a configured account to a channel. `file` uploads a file from your own node (an absolute path, up to 24 MiB), such as a plan's .md, with `text` as its message; `text` is optional with a file. `files` attaches inline text files, each {filename, text}. Discord and Slack take files, up to 10 MB on Discord and 8 MB on Tony's Slack. The Opal Slack bot refuses until its app holds files:write. Gmail and Teams refuse. `quiet` keeps the replies in the sent message's thread from its chat's seat holder. A bot account only.

functions.name: react
functions.description: Put an emoji reaction on a message, or take it off with `remove`. `emoji` is a character, a name or :name:. Discord and Slack react. Gmail and Teams refuse.

functions.name: fetch
functions.description: Fetch a channel's existing messages live from the platform (incl. ones from before the service started), with attachment metadata. `before` pages backwards. Nothing is stored — the platform is the source of truth.

functions.name: history
functions.description: Read a bot account's synced history of every chat the bot is in (edits applied, deletes hidden unless `include_deleted`). Newest `limit` messages, or with `since` (a message ts) the ones after it, oldest first — the catch-up read after `awm services listen social message`. Also lists each chat's sync cursor.

functions.name: seats
functions.description: List the chats a bot account is in (its seats), each with the session holding it or null. A session mounts a seat to have its messages typed into its prompt. `kept` is set on a seat a [seat.*] table declares: social starts and keeps its agent, with its job, health and restart count.

functions.name: mount
functions.description: Hold a seat: every new message in that chat, from anyone but the bot, is typed into your prompt as one line 'slack from <sender> [channel=<id> message_id=<id>]: <text>' (Discord: 'discord from'). Background sessions only. One holder per seat: a held seat is refused unless `force`, which takes it and tells the old holder. A Discord DM is a seat only for an operator, and a kept seat is refused: social holds it for the agent it keeps. The result's `rename` gives the seat's session name, seat:<app>/<server>/<channel>.

params.name: channel
params.description: A seat's id or name, as `seats` lists it.

functions.name: keepers
functions.description: List the kept seats ([seat.*] in social.toml): each one's agent, health (running, waiting, resuming, broken, ...), the reason, since when it is down and why, its recent resumes and restarts, and its last outage.

functions.name: keep_reset
functions.description: Clear a kept seat's breaker. A seat whose restarts kept failing is broken and is not tried again until this, or until six hours pass.

functions.name: keep_adopt
functions.description: Make a running background job the agent of a kept seat, keeping its conversation: for a holder started by hand that social keeps from now on.

functions.name: unmount
functions.description: Release a seat you hold, or every seat you hold on the account when `channel` is omitted.

functions.name: search
functions.description: Search a platform's own message index live (Slack search.messages, Gmail X-GM-RAW, Teams best-effort). Returns matches with attachment metadata. Not supported for Discord bot accounts (use fetch).

functions.name: download_attachments
functions.description: Download a message's attachments to a fresh temp dir on the node you call from (outside the awm workspace). Re-fetches the message live; returns `dir` and each file's `path`, `filename`, `mime`, `size`. Files together may not pass 24 MiB. `idx` optionally selects a single attachment.

functions.name: accounts
functions.description: List configured accounts with platform, kind, and live status.

functions.name: channels
functions.description: List channels visible to a configured account. `include_dms=true` also enumerates direct/group DMs (kind 'dm'/'group') where the platform supports it.

functions.name: open_dm
functions.description: Resolve a platform user (by id, or by name where the platform supports it) to a direct-message channel and open it. Returns the channel for use with fetch/send.

functions.name: list_operators
functions.description: List whitelisted operators, optionally by platform.

functions.name: add_operator
functions.description: Whitelist a platform user and map them to an awm_user.

functions.name: remove_operator
functions.description: Remove a platform user from the whitelist.

functions.name: lookup
functions.description: Resolve a (platform, user id) to its awm_user (or null).

functions.name: buckets
functions.description: List configured cloud file-store buckets (Google Drive, OneDrive/SharePoint) with kind and root. Each is probed now: `live` is false, with an `error`, when the store does not answer (e.g. a SharePoint session that needs re-authentication on mira).

functions.name: bucket_ls
functions.description: List the immediate children of a folder in a bucket. `path` is relative to the bucket root (omit for root). A OneDrive bucket also takes an absolute server-relative path (/teams/<site>/..., /sites/<site>/..., /personal/<user>/...) to reach any site the session can. A missing path is a not-found error, a file is a not-a-folder error. Returns entries with name, path, is_dir, size, mime, web_url. `recursive=true` walks the whole tree instead, stopping at `limit` entries (default 1000) and setting `truncated` when more exist.

functions.name: bucket_stat
functions.description: Return the entry for one file or folder in a bucket, or a not-found error. Paths as for bucket_ls.

functions.name: bucket_mkdir
functions.description: Create the folder at `path` in a bucket, with every missing parent. Succeeds on an existing folder. Paths as for bucket_ls.

functions.name: bucket_get
functions.description: Download a file from a bucket to a system temp dir (outside the awm workspace) on the node social runs on and return its absolute path + metadata. Any size; it streams in chunks. Google-native docs are exported (Docs→pdf, Sheets→csv). A folder downloads as a local folder tree (files[0].is_dir, with `count` files), refusing one over `limit` entries (default 10000). Files that fail are listed in `failures` and the rest still download. `version` (a label from bucket_versions) reads an older version of a file.

functions.name: bucket_put
functions.description: Upload a file (`src` = a path on the node social runs on) to `path` in a bucket, creating or overwriting it. Any size; it streams in chunks. A local folder uploads as the folder `path`, its tree inside it; files that fail are listed in `failures` and the rest still upload. `parents=true` creates missing folders above `path`; without it a missing folder is a not-found error. Returns the resulting entry.

functions.name: bucket_rm
functions.description: Delete the file/folder at `path` in a bucket.

functions.name: bucket_mv
functions.description: Move or rename the file or folder `src` to `dst` in a bucket. `dst` is the full new path, not a folder to move into. Paths as for bucket_ls, so a OneDrive move may cross sites (the name stays the same across sites). Version history and sharing go with the item. An existing `dst` is an error unless `overwrite=true`, which first sends it to the recycle bin (Drive: trash). `parents=true` creates missing folders above `dst`. Returns the new entry.

functions.name: bucket_cp
functions.description: Copy the file or folder `src` to `dst` in a bucket. Arguments and errors as for bucket_mv. Returns the new entry.

functions.name: bucket_sites
functions.description: Discover where a OneDrive bucket can reach. Without `site`: the personal OneDrive, the SharePoint sites search finds (minutes behind a new site) and followed sites. With `site` (e.g. /teams/<x>): that site's document libraries. Each entry has name, an absolute path to pass to the other bucket verbs, kind (personal, site, library) and web_url.

functions.name: bucket_versions
functions.description: List the versions of a file in a OneDrive bucket, newest first: label, size, modified, author, and which one is current. Read one with bucket_get `version`, bring one back with bucket_restore.

functions.name: bucket_restore
functions.description: Undo in a OneDrive bucket. With `version`: make that version of the file at `path` current again (the replaced one stays in the history). With `recycled=true`: bring back the item deleted from `path` (a path now occupied is an error). With neither: list the recycle bin at or below `path` (default the bucket root), newest first, up to `limit` (default 500).

functions.name: bucket_share
functions.description: Share a file or folder in a OneDrive bucket. CAUTION: this is outward-facing. Get Tony's explicit confirmation of the item, the audience and the role before you call it. `scope`: organization (a link anyone at UBC can open, the default), people (direct access for the emails in `people`) or anyone (an anonymous link, if the tenant allows it). `role`: view (default) or edit. `send_email` (default false) mails the people. Returns the url.

functions.name: bucket_shares
functions.description: List the share links on a file or folder in a OneDrive bucket (url, scope, role) and the people with access (name, email, role).

functions.name: bucket_unshare
functions.description: Revoke one share link (`link` = its url or share id, from bucket_shares) or one person's access (`person` = an email) on a file or folder in a OneDrive bucket. Pass exactly one of the two.

functions.name: bucket_resolve
functions.description: Turn a SharePoint/OneDrive share link (https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/:f:/t/<site>/<token>) into the entry it points at, with a path the other bucket verbs take. Not-found when the session cannot see the item.

functions.name: bucket_search
functions.description: Search a bucket for files matching `query` (Google Drive: name match across the drive; OneDrive: SharePoint search, scoped to the bucket root or to `path`). Returns matching entries.

functions.name: emit_probe
functions.description: Emit a synthetic, inert `command` event carrying only `nonce`, so a subscriber can prove on demand that it can still receive. Opens no window, arms nothing, sends no message.
